exclusion_reason.message: WAFT/Twins is carried as CPU-only, validated-but-unmeasured evidence (decision 2C). The selected zero-shot.pth checkpoint member has no published file-level commercial-use or redistribution terms (models/waft-twins-artifact.json), so shipping and OFX selection remain blocked pending an explicit checkpoint terms review. The Linux x86_64 ONNX artifact identity fields are bound to the validated linux-x86_64 manifest (models/waft-twins-artifact.json) from the on-box WAFT validation-export run, whose export is a fixed 128x192 spatial shape: WAFT specializes resolution and cannot export a spatially-dynamic ONNX (no dynamic-shape support). It is therefore NOT scheduled in the shared mp0_331776 (768x432) lattice — a 128x192 graph cannot accept the lattice input, and 128x192 matches no protocol cap token. models/export_waft.py exposes only CPUExecutionProvider, so measurement_providers is [cpu] and the candidate is CPU-only. A full arena measurement would require a re-export at the lattice resolution plus a CUDA validation pack, which is deferred.

NeuFlow v2 is a shipping-candidate carried for measurement only, and is restricted by the frozen protocol candidate_constraints to cap mp0_331776 (768x432, canonical 16:9). The neuflow_mixed.pth checkpoint has no checkpoint-specific license (models/neuflow-v2.json), so shipping and OFX selection remain blocked pending a checkpoint terms review. The Linux x86_64 ONNX artifact identity fields are now bound to the validated linux-x86_64 manifest (models/neuflow-v2.json) from the on-box NeuFlow validation-export run. That validation was CPU-only, so the checked-in NeuFlow evidence is CPU-only and measurement_providers is [cpu]; NeuFlow GPU (CUDA) measurement is deferred until an explicit NeuFlow CUDA qualification run produces a returned report carrying measurement_providers cuda.

Original RAFT is a validation-baseline only. The frozen P25 protocol admits it purely as a validation baseline: it can never receive an OFX choice, ship, or win the ranking, and its official checkpoint has no published commercial-use or redistribution terms (models/raft-original.json). It is CPU-only here; CUDA would require an explicit EL8 requalification not claimed by its manifest. Its Linux ONNX is CI-fetched and reproducibly exported (models/fetch_raft_checkpoint.py), so the identity fields use the materialize-from-linux-manifest CI pattern.
